item.title: Re: Easily Missed? Giant cell arteritis
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor I read the article on Giant Cell Arteritis BMJ 7-14 February 2026 with interest. Educationally it was excellent. However I was dismayed that in an article that so often mentions visual loss, the TABUL study was described as "blinded". Can reviewers and editors please adopt and insist on the term "masked" instead? Thank you. Mark Batterbury Consultant Ophthalmologist St. Paul's Eye Unit Liverpool UK No competing Interests: YesThe following competing Interests:

item.title: Re: Reliability of urological telesurgery compared with local surgery: multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Wang and colleagues present an important and timely randomised controlled trial evaluating the reliability of urological telesurgery. It provides essential prospective evidence in a field that has historically relied on small feasibility studies and case series. item.title: Climate imperatives are driving renewed interest in nuclear power — but in an era of hybrid warfare, nuclear expansion also creates distinct public‑health vulnerabilities.
